I've seen one or two labeled as "troll" when perhaps rude, crude, imature or coarse would be better descriptors. With the latest influx from the previous iteration, allot of us are on "high alert" for trolls, but is that really fare?
Where is the line between rudeness and trolling? Can we reliably tell the difference?

Rude, crude, immature, and coarse are the very hallmarks of a seasoned troll. Their remarks are intended to be inflammatory as well as incite a negative response.

If you encounter someone acting that way, your best course of action is to ignore them and go about your business. Nothing good will come of any further exchange. Hopefully we will soon have to ability to block users. That should make things easier.

Yes, I'm all for being able to block individuals. And I do agree that trolls are often rude, crude etc, but is that what makes them a troll? I had thought that trolls were those that were trying to make people mad, not just people that are rude. I mean, rudeness isn't always unjustified, and isn't always a poor tool for communication is it? or is it?

I've seen a few "anti-troll" people on here that are pretty rude, even if they try to disguise it.

So now that I'm thinking about it, maybe "troll" really does just mean "rude". If that's the case though, we should just say "you're rude" rather than "you're a troll", as I think some people who are largely considered trolls don't think they are. They are just "telling it like it is" (which is just an excuse to justify being hurtful).

In my opinion, a troll is anyone who attempts to elicit an emotional response by being overly rude, negative, controversial, or insulting. For example, I don't know you. So why would I desire to upset you in any way?

In short, I wouldn't. It makes no sense.

Having said that, I realize there are also people who lack a social filter. They say whatever they want, whenever they want with no thought or care to how it might affect others.

So, what are your thoughts in these cases? They care nothing for how they might make others feel, but at the same time expect everyone to cater to their own feelings and desires, no matter how outlandish they may seem to some of us.

So now, you have me thinking. That's a good thing. :)

I feel that some of the people I've met in person who have little to no social filters end up being some of the more intelligent/insightful people I've met. That being said, these folks are few and far between. Hell, I can be pretty crass if I'm feeling comfortable with the company I have at the time, though my personal intelligence and insight is questionable at best.

I think there are some folks that are just trolls, out to stir shit up and piss people off, and that is their only intention. Downvoat and ignore.

I think there are some folks that troll when they get pissed, or defensive (are just being rude).

I think there are some folks that have limited social skills and appear to be trolling, but actually have some intelligent things to say once in a while.

I'm pretty sure I'm not a Troll. :D

You made some excellent points! So, we are left with various shades of grey.

Still, if the conversation goes awry, I believe the only reasonable recourse is to walk away. There is no reason to think that once someone gets overly-defensive, rude, or nasty that anything we may say will change their viewpoint. Anything we reply with will just make them more upset. It quickly becomes a no win situation.
